Redirect those funds to incentivize doctors to practice in underserved areas instead of creating new administrative layers. The FARM Act already protects rural interests—enforce it.

The real shame? California’s Medicaid system is a bloated mess of bureaucratic waste, not a model of efficiency. Over 60% of CA-13 relies on Medi-Cal because D.C. prioritizes dependency over sustainable solutions.

Reform starts with accountability, not blank checks for failed programs.

Real compassion means dismantling dependency pipelines and forcing DC to prioritize efficiency over vote-buying handouts.

This bipartisan bill claims to fix Medicare reimbursement rates, but let’s cut through the spin. The Protecting Patient Access to Cancer and Complex Therapies Act is just another band-aid on a bullet wound—D.C. created this mess by kneecapping Part B drug payments through the Inflation Reduction Act’s reckless pricing controls. Now they’re scrambling to undo their own damage while pretending to champion patient access.

Real reform would dismantle the IRA’s entire price-setting scheme crushing innovation, not tweak reimbursement formulas to appease bureaucrats. Medicare’s cancer drug spending dropped $56B under these policies, forcing providers to ration care.

This bill doesn’t solve systemic waste—it just shifts the grift from one government failure to another. Until Washington stops rigging healthcare for Pharma profits and hospital monopolies, patients will keep losing.

Congressman Gray’s STRIVE Act highlights a critical issue: veterans shouldn’t pay for VA’s administrative failures. But let’s dig deeper. The Veterans Affairs Transfer of Information and Sharing of Disability Examination Procedures With DOD Doctors Act (H.R. 555) already mandates joint DoD-VA medical recordkeeping to prevent these exact bureaucratic delays.

While limiting copays is commendable, the real fix is streamlining systems to eliminate errors upfront. The VA’s $2.9B IT budget hasn’t stopped endless processing delays—yet H.R. 555 forces interoperability, reducing the need for retroactive copay relief.

Accountability matters, but so does preventing failures. Let’s pass bills that attack the root cause, not just the symptoms.

Congressional gridlock keeps veterans trapped in broken systems—see the full analysis: https://t.co/QTEw95caX6
